executive_assessment.text: Named evidence differentiates Grodno/Brest seasonal hydrology, Gomel/Pripyat water stress, Kopyl rural water access and a Brahin farm case.
Polesie evidence concerns interacting drought, floods, drained peatlands and radioactive-contamination risks. Its environmental-security framing is not a climate-caused violence finding.
Dated sector plans, peatland work and one supported farm illustrate reported capacities. Targets and institutional statements are not verified national adaptation or peace outcomes.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2020-12-18 reports: OECD reports earlier spring runoff nationwide since the 1980s; cited records show maximum spring runoff fell 43% on average between 1877–1965 and 1966–2005, with Grodno more affected than Brest oblast.

Source dated 2020-12-18 reports: OECD reports that Pripyat runoff during Gomel's growing season could decline by up to 25% by 2035, partly due to climate-linked precipitation decline, intensifying seasonal water stress for agriculture.

Source dated 2020-12-18 reports: In Kopyl rayon, OECD reports centralized water access for 98% of Kopyl town residents but 27% across rural settlements; many small communities rely on shallow wells with limited routine water-quality checks.

Source dated 2020 reports: The UNCCD article reports 7.9 mm of rain in Homiel during the April 2020 planting season, 19% of normal, and says roughly 45% of the region lies in the Chornobyl-contaminated zone, making peat fires a public-health concern.

Source dated 2020 reports: UNCCD reports about 1,000 ha of degraded peatland rewetted in Mogilev region in 2018–2019 with local-authority, forestry and community partnership; its 2020 Homiel phase targeted at least 2,000 ha and improved fire monitoring and early warning.

Source dated 2024-09-10 reports: Farmers interviewed in Brahin district report near-annual heatwaves causing drought, water shortages and crop failures; late May or June frosts require protective crop covering and add costs.

Source dated 2024-09-10 reports: Three sisters running a Brahin farm diversified and rotated crops, shifted grains toward drought-resilient winter cereals, and used an EU–UNDP-supported greenhouse with ventilation, heating and watering systems.

known_gaps.text: No reviewed source provides current subnational conflict or violence data linked to climate exposure in Belarus; the OSCE assessment is a 2017 regional risk analysis, not incident attribution.

The UNFCCC review records Belarus's statement that sanctions pressure ended some bilateral hydrometeorological data-exchange agreements, but does not identify partners or show resulting adaptation effects; this is not classified here as an explicit conflict link.
The 2025 VNR PDF was blocked and the 2026–2035 NDC was accessible only in Russian without substantive extraction; current status of plans reported in NC8 was not verified.
UNCCD's Homiel/Mogilev peatland project figures and UNDP's Brahin farm examples are reported by project-associated sources, not independent impact evaluations.
General environmental, health and livelihood security is not automatically FCV evidence. No full climate-FCV pathway is assembled.
Reported sanctions-related data-sharing constraints are retained as attributed political/institutional context, without an unverified downstream adaptation outcome.
